name: Founding of Rome
description: The city of Rome is believed to be founded by Romulus and Remus.

name: Roman Republic
description: The Roman Republic is established, marking the end of the Roman Kingdom.

name: Punic Wars
description: A series of wars fought between Rome and Carthage, resulting in Roman dominance in the western Mediterranean.

name: Julius Caesar's Assassination
description: Julius Caesar, the Roman dictator, is assassinated by a group of senators led by Brutus.

name: Roman Empire
description: Augustus becomes the first Roman Emperor, establishing the Roman Empire.

name: Construction of the Colosseum
description: Construction of the iconic Colosseum in Rome is completed.

name: Edict of Milan
description: Emperor Constantine issues the Edict of Milan, granting religious freedom to Christians.

name: Sack of Rome
description: The Visigoths, led by Alaric, sack Rome, marking a significant decline in Roman power.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The Western Roman Empire falls as Romulus Augustus is deposed by Odoacer, marking the end of Ancient Rome.

name: Codification of Roman Law
description: Emperor Justinian I codifies Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis, laying the foundation for modern legal systems.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: The Eastern Roman Empire, known as the Byzantine Empire, continues to thrive after the fall of the Western Roman Empire.

name: Fall of Constantinople
description: The Ottoman Empire captures Constantinople, bringing an end to the Byzantine Empire.

name: Arch of Constantine
description: The Arch of Constantine is dedicated in Rome to commemorate Emperor Constantine's victory.

name: Roman Baths
description: The Romans develop sophisticated public bathing facilities known as Roman Baths.

name: Roman Road Network
description: The Romans build an extensive road network spanning across their empire, facilitating trade and military movements.

name: Roman Aqueducts
description: Roman engineers construct aqueducts to supply water to cities, showcasing their engineering prowess.

name: Roman Senate
description: The Roman Senate, a political institution, plays a crucial role in the governance of the Roman Republic and Empire.

name: Roman Literature
description: Roman authors such as Virgil, Cicero, and Ovid contribute to a rich body of literature in Latin.

name: Roman Architecture
description: Roman architects create grand structures like the Pantheon and the Roman Colosseum, showcasing their architectural prowess.

name: Roman Engineering
description: Roman engineers develop innovative engineering techniques, constructing impressive structures like roads, aqueducts, and bridges.

name: Roman Religion
description: Roman religion is a polytheistic belief system involving various gods and goddesses, with Emperor worship becoming prominent.

name: Roman Expansion
description: The Roman Empire expands its territory through military conquests, incorporating various regions into its domain.

name: Roman Coinage
description: The Romans introduce a standardized currency system, issuing coins that become widely used across the empire.

name: Roman Slavery
description: Slavery plays a key role in the Roman Empire's economy, with large numbers of enslaved people performing various tasks.

name: Division of the Roman Empire
description: The Roman Empire is divided into the Western Roman Empire and the Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantine Empire) for administrative purposes.
